crime: Every night at lockup, {WITCH_NAME} walked the cell corridor with a single cup of warm milk. In her hands it became two cups, then more, until that one cup was enough to pass through every barred cell door.
For weeks, one girl kept her company at the upper railing each dusk. Yet the girl turned down every copy {WITCH_NAME} offered her, even of the sleeping drug she took each night. "One is enough."
One dusk, after the others had gone in, the girl put her nightly pill in {WITCH_NAME}'s palm. "I slept without it. I won't need it anymore."
Long ago, when that palm was small, {WITCH_NAME}'s mother had put her own nightly pill back into it. "I don't need it anymore." By morning, her mother was gone.

There at the railing, the one pill became a handful in {WITCH_NAME}'s palm, all alike. At lockup she dropped the handful into the last cup and passed it through the girl's barred door, as she did every night.
At unlock, the prisoners found the girl lying still in her bunk bed. Two pills sat whole at the bottom of her cup.

In the trial court, the prisoners ruled that she had swallowed pills she'd been saving. {WITCH_NAME}, they said, had never once held the girl's pill. Then one prisoner noticed that the two pills from the cup had the same chipped corner. The prisoners understood: pills alike down to the chip were copies of a single pill, so {WITCH_NAME} had held the girl's pill after all.
fields.epitaph: She never could give just one.
fields.epithet: The Hand That Must Be Needed
execution: The execution stand raised a giant iron cup. She sat chained at its bottom. An iron hand tipped an iron pitcher over the rim, and the milk poured on and never ran dry. It rose over her chest, her chin, her mouth. She strained upward against the chain. Then the milk lay still to the brim, and nothing rose through it.

magic.name: One Into Many
magic.text: She can turn any nonliving thing she holds into several real, identical copies.
